svg.aria-label: chat-integration-protocol: how @growi/chat splits its public surface, drives the six-step pairing procedure, and signs and verifies every request with RFC 9421.
svg.text: @growi/chat — the shared contract, signature, and shape-check layer between GROWI and the chat proxy
1. One package, two entry points, one hard wall
Both processes import the same code; only server-side code may ever touch node:crypto.
a drift test proves index.ts can never statically reach node:crypto
2. Pairing — six steps, no keys until step 6
Steps 3-5 carry no signature; the registration code and challengeSignature are the only protection.
④ OwnershipChallenge → sent to the SUBMITTED growiUri
⑤ ChallengeResponse — only if pending code matches
⑥ PairingResult: verify challengeSignature → relationId + proxy's public key
The purpose-prefixed payload is why step ⑤ can never be tricked into
producing a real RFC 9421 request signature.
3. Every signed request after pairing — RFC 9421 over Ed25519
The destination URL and path are never covered, so op is the only thing binding a signature to a specific endpoint.
Where this fits, and how it was built
before proxy or app can start —
